When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT.

On this date, Pacific Time (PT) will be Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7. Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1, as European summer time ends the weekend before. This means Madrid is 8 hours ahead of PT. Adding 8 hours to 11:59 PM on Friday, October 30, pushes the time into the next morning in your location.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is on Monday, November 2, 2026, at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time. On that date, Los Angeles will be on Pacific Standard Time (UTC-8) and Madrid will be on Central European Time (UTC+1). This means Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles. Therefore, you must add 9 hours to the deadline time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts on Saturday, October 24, 2026, and lasts for 48 hours (two full days). This period includes the end of Daylight Saving Time in Spain, which occurs on Sunday, October 25, 2026, when clocks are set back by one hour. Because the hackathon's duration is 48 actual hours, and one hour is "gained" on the clock, the event will end one hour earlier than a simple two-day addition would suggest.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest starts on October 26, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT. At that time of year, Pacific Time is PDT (UTC-7), making the start time 17:00 UTC. The deadline is 72 hours (exactly 3 days) later, which is October 29, 2026, at 17:00 UTC.

In 2026, Spain transitions from summer time (CEST, UTC+2) back to standard time (CET, UTC+1) on October 25. Therefore, on the deadline date of October 29, Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1). Converting the 17:00 UTC deadline to your local time means adding one hour, making it 18:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

First, we need to determine the deadline in a universal time format, UTC. On October 31, 2026, the US is still on Daylight Saving Time, so ET refers to EDT, which is UTC-4. The deadline of 11:59 PM ET is therefore November 1, 2026, at 03:59 UTC.

Next, we calculate the announcement time by adding 36 hours. This brings us to November 2, 2026, at 15:59 UTC.

Finally, we convert this to your local time in Madrid. In November, Spain is on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1. Therefore, the announcement will be one hour ahead of the UTC time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The provided Unix timestamp corresponds to Saturday, August 1, 2026, at 09:39 UTC. Since your time zone in Tokyo is Japan Standard Time (JST), which is 9 hours ahead of UTC (UTC+9), we add 9 hours to find your local deadline.

ANSWER: 2026-08-01 18:39

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline `2026-10-25T02:30:00Z` is in UTC. Madrid is in the Central European Time zone (CET/CEST). In 2026, Daylight Saving Time ends on Sunday, October 25, at 01:00 UTC, when clocks change from UTC+2 to UTC+1. Since the deadline of 02:30 UTC is after this change, your local time will be on standard time (UTC+1).

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is set for 11:59 PM on October 25, 2026, Pacific Time. On this date, the US will be on Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7. This converts to 6:59 AM UTC on October 26.

In Europe, daylight saving ends on the last Sunday of October. Therefore, on October 26, Madrid will have switched back to Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1. Converting the UTC deadline to your local time gives you 7:59 AM on October 26.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In 2026, the United States ends Daylight Saving Time on Sunday, November 1. The deadline is at 12:00 noon Eastern Time on that day. At that time, the US East Coast will have returned to Eastern Standard Time (EST), which is UTC-5. Lima, Peru, is on Peru Time (PET) year-round, which is also UTC-5. Therefore, the time will be the same in both locations.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

"AoE" stands for "Anywhere on Earth," which is a timezone equivalent to UTC-12:00, the last place on Earth where a day ends. The time 24:00 on December 31 is the same moment as 00:00 on January 1. Therefore, the deadline is January 1, 2027, at 00:00 UTC-12. This converts to 12:00 UTC on January 1, 2027. Your local time in Tokyo is Japan Standard Time (JST), which is UTC+9. Adding 9 hours to the UTC deadline gives you the deadline in your local time.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Of course. To determine the deadline in your local time while you are in New York, we need to convert the time from Sydney.

On October 5, 2026, Sydney will be on Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT), which is 11 hours ahead of UTC (UTC+11). New York will be on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is 4 hours behind UTC (UTC-4). This means New York is 15 hours behind Sydney. Subtracting 15 hours from 5:00 PM on October 5th gives us the time in New York.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
